items.description: The stock_records Alembic migration downgrades one step then upgrades back cleanly under @pytest.mark.migration without downgrading to base
Records seeded before the additive stock_records migration survive it with their original column values intact
The database rejects a stock_records insert that supplies a null quantity
The database rejects a stock_records insert that supplies a null sku
The database rejects a stock_records insert that supplies a null location
The database rejects a stock_records insert that supplies a null inventory_code
The database CHECK rejects a stock_records insert where quantity is negative
Filing twice for the same (sku, location) pair against the real branch leaves exactly one stored row in stock_records
The boundary layer (app/routes/) contains no ORM or database session imports
Direct persistence and database session usage appears only in the repository layer (app/repositories/)
The service layer (app/services/) contains no ORM or session imports
The database connection string is read from the DATABASE_URL environment variable and is not hardcoded anywhere in the application
The integration test suite connects to the real paired branch database via DATABASE_URL
No in-memory or mocked database driver is present in the integration test suite
The app/routes boundary returns JSON responses with no server-side template rendering
POSTing a new stock record to the API with a unique SKU, location, quantity, and inventory_code results in the record being durably stored and a 2xx response returned
GETting a stock record via the API after it has been filed returns the exact quantity that was written
GETting a stock record via the API after it has been filed returns the exact combined inventory_code that was written
POSTing a second stock filing for the same SKU and location pair via the API returns a success response with no error surfaced
After two filings for the same SKU and location pair via the API, the API returns exactly one record for that pair
The service layer rejects a write that would drive the stored quantity below zero before it reaches the repository
The boundary validation error payload names the specific invalid field rather than returning a generic bad-request message
An in-place upsert for an existing (sku, location) leaves the stored created_at timestamp unchanged
A concurrent repeat file for the same (sku, location) stores exactly one row via the single-transaction upsert
<App> renders the stock filing page when MemoryRouter is initialised at the /stock/file route
The SKU input on the stock filing form carries its design-guide data-testid attribute
The location input on the stock filing form carries its design-guide data-testid attribute
The quantity input on the stock filing form carries its design-guide data-testid attribute
The inventory_code input on the stock filing form carries its design-guide data-testid attribute
Submitting the filing form with all valid field values issues a POST request to the stock API endpoint
<App> renders the stock record view when MemoryRouter is initialised at the /stock/:sku/:location route with a specific SKU and location
The quantity display element on the stock record view carries its design-guide data-testid attribute
The inventory_code display element on the stock record view carries its design-guide data-testid attribute
The quantity shown in the stock record view matches the value returned by the mocked API response
The inventory_code shown in the stock record view matches the value returned by the mocked API response
After a second form submission for the same SKU and location pair, no error banner or alert element is visible in the UI
After a second form submission for the same SKU and location pair, the form returns to a non-error success-indicating state
